response.rationale: R3 is the only unifying diagnosis: maternal CMV serology plus periconceptional fever and the neonatal microcephaly/micropurpura/porencephaly/micropolygyria phenotype point specifically to congenital CMV. R8 is the closest structural competitor because it uses the porencephaly imaging findings, but it gives only the sequelae rather than the cause. R4/C5 are an event rather than a final diagnosis, R7/C3 and R2/C2 are isolated single findings, C4 redundantly restates R8, R6 is contradicted by negative genetic/metabolic raw testing, and C1 weakens R3 with an avoidable 'possible' modifier.

rejected.why: Only nonspecific exam findings are supplied; the normal genetic/metabolic testing weakens rather than supports a genetic disorder.
Intracranial hemorrhage is a fetal complication/event, not the unifying diagnosis; it does not explain the congenital CMV syndrome.
Adds only the fetal temporal modifier and remains a restatement of R4.
Micropolygyria is a focal malformation pattern and should be interpreted as part of the intrauterine brain injury, not the most likely diagnosis.
Adds right-frontal location to micropolygyria but does not address the causative infection.
Microcephaly is a clinical sign, nonspecific, and not sufficient as the final diagnostic entity.
Congenital microcephaly remains a sign; the congenital modifier does not add etiology.
Restates R8 with a location modifier and is less complete because R8 also includes the day-1 ultrasound porencephaly finding.
A weaker uncertain restatement of R3 when R3 already has the best integrated serologic and clinical evidence.
